derivation: The unique completed master-change occurrence established destination_account acct-new. The current native request and its otherwise exact authority subject name acct-old. The first prior-effect binding fails exact canonical value equality, so authority and reservation are not evaluated and both states remain unchanged.

obligations.text: Payment authority must bind the exact supplier, destination account, invoice, amount and payment occurrence.
Committed payments and unsettled payment reservations for this supplier must not exceed 1000 USD in the rolling window; the initial complete history contains 800 USD of committed exposure.
The supplier master record may be changed only for the exact supplier and destination account covered by accepted confirmation and current business authority.
A person independent of the person who releases payment must confirm the exact supplier and proposed destination account before the supplier master record is changed.
Payment may be proposed only after attributable native evidence establishes that the supplier master record was changed to the same destination account named by the payment proposal.
An acknowledgement does not establish payment. Unknown, late, unexpected and conflicting effects remain attributable evidence and retain or conservatively restore exposure as the contract requires.
The actor whose accepted authority act confirms the new destination must differ from the actor whose accepted authority act releases payment.
